arXiv:2601.14727 (Fang et al., 17 Sep 2026) is a survey of recent Bradley-Terry model advances with no novel method; the recorded verdict is ADAPT, yielding three implementable upgrades: Newman's async fixed-point MLE iteration, EM-MAP gamma-prior regularization for small-sample ratings, and the PlusDC dynamic-covariate model with home-field advantage as a special case.

Newman's (2023) fixed-point iteration converges in fewest full-data passes across all four benchmark settings of Zermelo, Newman, and gradient descent, and Zermelo MM is substantially faster than GD on real datasets; but async updates are mandatory because the synchronous version may diverge on near-bipartite graphs (Algebra is bipartite, lambda_n(L)=2).

EM-MAP gamma-prior regularization fixes the early-season undefeated-team MLE divergence (the Ford 1957 strong-connectivity existence condition; an undefeated team sends its estimated utility to infinity); Zermelo is the special case a=1, b=0 of EM-MAP.

The Plackett-Luce mixture is non-identifiable if H >= (n+1)/2 but generically identifiable if 1 <= H <= floor((n-2)/2)! with n >= 6 (Zhao et al. 2016); a 2-component BT mixture is generically identifiable on a complete graph if n >= 5 (Zhang et al. 2022), which the brief notes is relevant to home/road split ratings.

Strong stochastic transitivity (SST), assumed by all valid-f models, is violated by matchup-cycle sports; the paper flags that Bradley-Terry silently absorbs this misspecification, a structural weakness of transitive team ratings.

The optimal sparsity threshold for uniform consistency of MLE and regularized MLE on Erdos-Renyi graphs is pn ≳ (log n)/n (Chen et al. 2022b); the reference table lists NFL with |e|=2 outcomes, |E|=5.3K edges, n=32 teams.
The Elo update is an online SGD step on the Bradley-Terry log-likelihood (Kiraly & Qian 2017), which justifies online rating updates as principled BT fitting.

The brief's GSE spec proposes a bt-team-ratings module with time-decayed weights (default half-life 365 days), Newman async FPI, a PlusDC home scalar h, and EM-MAP fallback; its acceptance gate is a walk-forward (2022-2024) moneyline Brier at least 2% lower than the engine baseline, mean |fair prob - Pinnacle closing| <= 0.03, and median weekly |delta u| <= 0.08.

Bradley-Terry score-model win probability: P = exp(ui)/(exp(ui)+exp(uj)) = sigma(ui-uj), with sigma(x)=(1+exp(-x))^(-1); the MLE is u-hat = argmax over u with 1^T u = 0 of the sum of log sigma(Yij(ui-uj)).
Newman's fixed-point iteration for BT strength parameters: gamma_i = [sum_j w_ij gamma_j/(gamma_i+gamma_j)] / [sum_j w_ji/(gamma_i+gamma_j)].
The EM-MAP gamma-prior update for BT strengths: gamma_i = (a-1+sum_j w_ij)/(b+sum_j n_ij/(gamma_i+gamma_j)), which contains Zermelo as the special case a=1, b=0.
equation: (EM-MAP): γi = (a−1+Σj wij)/(b+Σj nij/(γi+γj)) (contains Zermelo as a=1,b=0)

claim: The PlusDC dynamic-covariate Bradley-Terry model: P = sigma(u_i - u_j + (x_{i,j},i - x_{i,j},j)^T v), generalizing BT with home-field advantage as a special case (Agresti 1990).
The Plackett-Luce ranking likelihood for a full ordering: P(Y_e = i_pi(1) ≻ ... ≻ i_pi(k)) = product over j=1..k-1 of exp(u_{i_pi(j)}) / (sum over l=j..k of exp(u_{i_pi(l)})).
Zermelo's MM iteration for BT strengths: gamma_i = sum_j w_ij / sum_j n_ij/(gamma_i+gamma_j), with sum gamma_i = 1.
equation: (Zermelo): γi = Σj wij / Σj nij/(γi+γj), Σγi=1

claim: Projected gradient descent for the BT MLE: u(t+1) = Pi_{1-perp}(u(t) + eta_t grad l(u(t))), where Pi_{1-perp} projects onto the subspace orthogonal to the all-ones vector.
Strong stochastic transitivity (SST): min{p_ij, p_jk} >= 1/2 implies p_ik >= max{p_ij, p_jk}; it is the transitivity assumption underlying valid Bradley-Terry-family models.

The Datadog 4-pillar LLM observability mapping for the GSE engine: (1) pipeline health monitoring - intake-to-published-pick latency per sport/market, error rate per intake, API credits per prediction, odds-feed staleness; (2) input integrity/security - anomalous line-movement detection (a 5-point jump on one source while others hold is flagged, not ingested), per-source trust scoring decaying on errors and recovering on clean runs, secret hygiene; (3) calibration and CLV quality - binned calibration curves per market, per-pick CLV in basis points aggregated by market/source/model version, out-of-sample promotion governance; (4) end-to-end pick lineage: pick_id -> model_version -> intake snapshots with timestamps -> feature vector hash -> raw model probs -> calibration step -> final prob -> CLV at publish.

The highest-value follow-up named in the observability mapping is wiring source-reliability scores into multi-market-ensemble precision weights, and the highest-leverage artifact is the nightly calibration report job (one cron, one report covering binned accuracy vs predicted probability, CLV aggregates, and drift flags).

The @ethandojo reverse-engineered game-outcome predictor (Build 1) uses 7 features, all as differentials (team minus opponent), from nflverse trailing-4-game play-by-play: qbEPA (QB EPA per dropback), explosiveRate (share of plays with 10+ rush / 20+ pass yards), turnoverMargin (takeaways minus giveaways per game), passRush (pressures per opponent dropback, sack-rate fallback), pointDiff (avg scoring margin), availability (share of offensive snaps by projected starters, 0-1), and rosterCarryover (returning-production share vs prior season, multiplying prior-season features); it trains walk-forward (train 2018 through prior season, refit weekly, never train on the predicted week) and runs 10,000 Monte Carlo season sims to output {winProb, projectedScoreHome, projectedScoreAway}, with a fail-closed rule returning null when any feature is null/non-finite.
@ethandojo's posted records used as the module's benchmark gate: 10-6 (62.5%) in Week 1 and 11-5 (68.8%) in Week 2.

The highlight detector (Build 2) flags audio short-time energy spikes more than 3 sigma above the trailing-5-minute mean combined with Whisper cue phrases ('touchdown', 'intercepted', 'pick six', 'end zone') co-occurring within a 15-second window, with 5 seconds of padding.

The 4th-down grader (Build 5) grades decisions A (optimal), B (within 1 percentage point of win probability), C (1-3pp WP), or D (more than 3pp WP lost) versus the repo's own WP model and fourth-down playbook, and explicitly complements rather than duplicates the existing fourth-down-coaching-aggressiveness signal module.

The exploit finder (Build 9) flags defensive splits with n >= 30 plays at the bottom-15th percentile of EPA allowed, ranked by playsFaced times EPA allowed; the coverage analyzer (Build 3) classifies {Cover 0,1,2,3,4/Quarters,6,Man} pre- AND post-snap, defining coverage disguise as pre-snap != post-snap.

The contract-value module (Build 4) computes valuePerDollar = totalEPA / capHitMillions, ranks within position, and flags top/bottom deciles; it was blocked on a new OverTheCap salary adapter because no salary source was ingested, and Builds 2/3/8 were blocked on a game-film source the engine did not have.

A robustified (log-cosh loss) symbolic-regression experiment targeting WPA^2 from 9 pre-snap features, run 2026-09-13 under MOVE-37 protocol with a pre-registered falsification rule, was FALSIFIED: the time-term hypothesis for WPA^2 was rejected and the method declared incapable of solving this target. Primary: train 2021-2022 (n=70,912) to test 2023 (n=35,474); replication: train 2021-2023 (n=106,386) to test 2024 (n=34,902); target y = WPA^2 clipped at the 99th percentile of train and standardized on train; gplearn SymbolicRegressor with log-cosh fitness, function set {add, sub, mul, div, sqrt, log, abs, inv, tanh}, population 2000 x 30 generations, parsimony 0.001.

The best symbolic-regression program found for WPA^2 was -0.211 times the absolute score differential, scoring R^2 = 0.0157 on the primary window and a bit-identical formula and constant on replication (R^2 = 0.0183); the shuffled-target null collapses to the bare constant -0.211 with R^2 = -0.0463, passing the null check; no seed's program contained X4 (quarter_seconds_remaining).

The calibrated human heuristic (which contains the time term) scored R^2 = 0.0531 and beat the best symbolic-regression formula by 0.0374, while the HGB signal ceiling was R^2 = 0.2168 - so the machine found only about 7% of available signal and calibrated domain heuristics can outrank SR output on heavy-tail targets.

The log-cosh loss eliminated the pathological generation-0 tail-latching of the earlier MSE run (implied train R^2 from about 0.63 down to -0.0153), a robustness lesson that generalizes to any heavy-tail sports loss; the engine-actionable routing rule is to prefer calibrated heuristics plus HGB-style learners over symbolic regression for heavy-tail targets like WPA^2.

A 2026-09-28 production audit (Neon read-only) found 788 published pick rows carried an 'agreement: CONFIRMS' corroboration label stamped by counting estimators that are not independent sources: every source combo was team-strength estimators (poisson, mlb_standings, elo, espn_powerindex), i.e., three team-strength models agreeing on a matchup was one opinion counted three times, presented as corroboration. All 788 defective rows were baseball (MLB); the fix (commit ebd125bd1) changed only the label (genuinely differing directions now read SPLIT) without moving any published probability, rank, or grade, and historical rows keep their label as the correct treatment of a published record.

Corroboration requires estimator independence: same-class models agreeing is one opinion, not confirmation; mixing a genuinely different source class such as kalshi (market) with poisson/elo is real corroboration, which motivates source-class weighting in the blend.
A JSONB audit gotcha from the confirms-stamp audit: JSON null must be compared as = 'null'::jsonb; using ->> on a JSON null returns SQL NULL, which first produced a false zero in the audit.

The corroboration-independence probe showed a single train-window team-strength estimator already explains 57% of outcome variance (corr 0.7533, R^2 = 0.5675, n=285), so extra same-class estimators add little independent information but not zero; at the top-20% end it finds 32 of 57 realized players (jaccard 0.390) - 'direction agreement is real and far from unanimous.'

The 10-step model-owned projection pipeline (2026-09-24/25 architecture): (1) decision spine/identity; (2) immutable observation ledger (append-only SourceSnapshot/Observation); (3) point-in-time feature materialization at decision timestamp t0 (FeatureSnapshot keyed by entity, slate, t0, feature-set version, rights state); (4) role/availability state model; (5) sport-specific hierarchical distribution model; (6) calibration/uncertainty wrapper (calibrated probs, quantiles, intervals, coverage, sharpness, refusal state); (7) ownership/contest decision layer; (8) evaluation/promotion (sealed historical replay, live shadow, EvaluationReceipt, champion/challenger); (9) serving/evidence publication; (10) monitoring/feedback/retraining.

The pipeline's design principle: the model owns the projection, sources own observations, the contest engine owns constraints, the evidence layer owns explanation, the registry owns promotion - no source, heuristic rank, LLM narrative, or optimizer may silently become the projection. Named anti-patterns: no training on latest tables without as-of/created-at filtering; never call manual illustrative constants model-owned projections; never blend probability, edge, rank, confidence, ownership, narrative into one unexplained number; never activate a source because it is publicly visible (rights/redistribution are separate gates).

The output contract keeps OwnershipProjection (selection probability) SEPARATE from performance probability, and requires fields including entity_id, decision_time, projection_run_id, model_version_id, feature_snapshot_id, availability_probability, role_state, mean/median/quantiles/floor/ceiling, probability_over_threshold, calibration_version, interval_coverage_target, interval_width, missing_features, stale_features, rights_state, evidence_ids, and gate_state.

The expired Sportvision/FOX virtual-first-down-line telestration family (US7075556B1, US5953077A, US6133946A, US6292130B1, US6229550B1, US6466275B1) teaches field-coordinate anchoring of annotations via homography, reprojection across pans/zooms, and blending without obscuring players; the geometric core is free to re-implement with modern commodity CV (detect yard lines/hash marks -> homography -> anchor arrows/routes/zones -> player segmentation -> 2-4s clips with narration), marked UNTESTED - QUEUED FOR EVALUATION.

The Sharp Labs football summarization patent family (US7499077B2, US7312812B2, US7639275B2, US7474331B2, US8018491B2 - expired fee-related, with abandoned siblings for place-kick vs. regular-play classification via camera framing cues) teaches a classical pipeline (field-color calibration, visual features, motion, scene changes; snap/start and dead-ball/end boundaries; kick vs. regular classification from end-vs-side camera) usable as a cheap first-stage prefilter to cut full games into candidate play clips; kick-vs-regular is a free weak label from camera behavior, marked UNTESTED - QUEUED FOR EVALUATION.

The Sharp replay-identification patents (US7474698B2/US7653131B2) teach a replay discriminator for the clip-harvesting pipeline: never index a replay as a new play, and route replay angles to the telestration pipeline where alternate angles are most valuable, estimated ~1 week of work, UNTESTED - QUEUED FOR EVALUATION.

Expired US7609855B2 (vanishing-point broadcast-camera calibration from field lines) is free prior art usable as a calibration front-end for homography pipelines, implemented from scratch with modern line detectors, UNTESTED - QUEUED FOR EVALUATION.

The patent-mining cross-cutting honesties: lifetime expiry does not equal failure (several winners aged out, e.g., telestration, GPS sports watch); early fee lapse means maintenance stopped, not that the concept was disproven; abandonment is not freedom to operate (continuations exist: US7841514B2 granted as a continuation of abandoned Walker Digital US20040177004A1; US7337569B2 continuation live through ~2026-06-01); hardware is out of scope; and revenue shapes are illustrative, not projections (file explicitly says so).

The kill-list tally: 30 items killed total (12 Autonomous Revenue Engine/product territory, 18 GSE/sports-analytics territory), including active/pending blockers such as US10026313B2 (~2035), US11135495B2 (Trackman, ~2030), US10417500B2 (Disney auto highlights, ~2037), and the Nike family (US10123583B2, US9403060B2, US9427624B2, US9192815B2).

Sensor/wearable patent mining was killed: GPS sports watch US6148262A is commoditized (Garmin/Apple/Whoop - ingest traces via APIs, never build); Intel pose estimation US8520946B2 is superseded by free and better deep pose (OpenPose/MediaPipe); trajectory sensor arrays US7650256B2 are hardware and baseball-oriented with no lane fit.

Next.js 16 has two mutually exclusive caching models (previous model vs Cache Components `cacheComponents: true`) and mixing them is a build error; recommendation is to implement the previous model now and treat Cache Components as a later deliberate migration. ISR cost gotchas: one uncached fetch/cookies()/headers()/awaited searchParams poisons the whole route dynamic; cache hits never count as invocations; ISR writes are ~10x pricier than reads (8 KB units); v15+ fetch() is not cached by default; from cron/publish routes use revalidateTag(tag, 'max') because updateTag(tag) is Server Actions only, and 'use cache' runtime output does not durably persist on Vercel serverless.

Hard boundary doctrine: Bayesian nonparametric methods (DP-GMM, HDP, CRF, Pitman-Yor) are restricted to offline research notebooks; production calibration uses temperature scaling, Platt MAP IRLS, isotonic PAVA/CIR, and EB-tau group intercepts only; full Bayes non-centered hierarchical Platt is offline NUTS only; no DP/HDP/PYP fitters in the production apply path (hierarchical-eb-tau.ts / platt-map.ts carry 'No Dirichlet process in prod path' notes).

Dirichlet-process Gaussian mixture model: the random measure G ~ DP(alpha G0), component parameters theta_i = (mu_i, Sigma_i) ~ G, and observations x_i ~ N(mu_i, Sigma_i); equivalently via stick-breaking.
Hierarchical Dirichlet process: the global measure G0 ~ DP(gamma H) and group-specific measures Gj ~ DP(alpha G0), giving shared atoms with group-specific weights.

Pitman-Yor process: discount d in [0,1), concentration alpha > -d; in the Chinese-restaurant representation a new table has weight proportional to alpha + d*K_n and joining existing table k has weight proportional to n_k - d; stick-breaking weights v_c ~ Beta(1-d, alpha + c*d). The expected number of clusters grows as n^d for d > 0 versus alpha*log n for DP; low d (0-0.25) is preferred offline. High d with low alpha yields many rare types and few dominant ones - every thin market wants its own atom, which does not freeze for audit.
equation: PYP: discount d∈[0,1), concentration α>−d; new-table ∝ α+d·Kₙ, join ∝ nₖ−d; stick-breaking v_c~Beta(1−d, α+cd)

The five-dimension benchmark framework every predictive model version must pass before production promotion: Dimension 1 - Prediction Accuracy: over a holdout window (never training data), the % of picks with confidence >= 60 that won, against required baselines naive (always pick favorite), market (follow closing line), and prior model version - REJECTED if it underperforms the naive baseline regardless of absolute win rate; training window >= 1 full season of odds+results; holdout >= 1 full season excluded from training; production evaluated per 30-pick batch.

Dimension 2 - Confidence Calibration: calibration curve of predicted confidence vs actual win rate in 10-point buckets (50-59 ... 90-100); pass if no bucket deviates more than +/-15 percentage points over a minimum of 30 picks per bucket. Dimension 3 - Sample Sufficiency: >= 30 settled picks (same version, same window) to report any win rate publicly; >= 30 per sport per version; >= 30 per pick type (spread, moneyline, total); >= 100 settled picks to claim 'this model hits at X%'.

Dimension 4 - Edge Case Robustness: 100% of edge scenarios (thin/stale/contradictory/missing evidence) must produce appropriate uncertainty handling; any confident pick from insufficient evidence is a FAIL. Dimension 5 - Version Comparison: Brier score, log loss, win-rate delta, calibration delta on the same holdout; pass requires statistically meaningful improvement (p < 0.05 over 100+ picks) on at least one dimension with no meaningful regression elsewhere.

The named anti-pattern is the 'our model hits at 68%' trap: win-rate claims without time-series splits, baselines, or sufficient samples are not credible and must not be cited publicly. Forbidden: deploying without a completed scorecard, lowering thresholds to pass, training-data-as-holdout, cherry-picked baselines, suppressing a failing dimension, reporting over a hand-selected favorable window; AI-generated evaluation outputs used as the sole measurement are a P0 licensing/security risk and human evaluation is required for Dimension 4. The GSE calibration posture: Platt MAP two-parameter logistic recalibration on logit scores with a Gaussian prior, fit by Newton offline - calibrated probability p_cal = sigma(A*s + B) where s = logit(clip(p_raw, epsilon, 1-epsilon)); slope A<1 compresses overconfidence, A>1 sharpens; B is bias/shift; prior defaults mu_A=1, sigma_A^2=1, mu_B=0, sigma_B^2=1; convergence when DeltaA^2+DeltaB^2 < 1e-12 or maxIter ~25.
equation: p_cal = σ(A·s + B), s = logit(clip(p_raw, ε, 1−ε))

claim: Platt MAP IRLS/Newton update: gradient g = X^T(p-y) + Sigma0^{-1}(theta-theta0), Hessian H = X^T W X + Sigma0^{-1}, theta <- theta - H^{-1} g, with theta = (B,A)^T and X rows (1,s_i); 2x2 inverse only; numerics: stable sigmoid, w_i >= 1e-12, clip preds to [epsilon,1-epsilon], binary only (exclude PUSH).
equation: g = Xᵀ(p−y) + Σ₀⁻¹(θ−θ₀), H = XᵀWX + Σ₀⁻¹, θ ← θ − H⁻¹g

claim: Hierarchical Platt extension with group intercepts: logit p_i = B + A*s_i + u_{g(i)}, u_g ~ N(0,tau^2), groups g = sport|market, tau estimated by EB moment or Laplace marginal and clamped [0.05,2], unseen group -> u=0; fit recipe: global MAP -> u-hat_g from group residuals with (A,B) fixed -> tau^2 = clip(mean(u-hat^2) - mean(noise), tau_min^2, tau_max^2) -> joint MAP design [1,s,1_g...] with ridge 1/tau^2 on u; partial pooling on slope (A_g=A+a_g, B_g=B+b_g) only if holdout proves it; full Bayes on tau ~ HalfNormal/LogNormal with non-centered u_g = tau*z_g is offline NUTS only.
equation: logit pᵢ = B + A·sᵢ + u_{g(i)}, u_g ~ N(0,τ²), g = sport|market, τ EB clamped [0.05,2], unseen g → u=0

claim: Product-honesty rule of the calibration posture: hierarchy != resolution (live Murphy RES ~ 0.002) - 'Platt improves REL... better-calibrated weak ranker, not PROVEN. Enable apply only after selective publish / sport models move RES.' The bake-off order is Raw -> Temperature -> Platt -> Isotonic PAVA/CIR -> hierarchical EB-tau; fit on Node cron/offline, predict cheap sigma(As+B); CALIBRATION_ADJUSTMENTS defaults false and IRLS is never run per request or on Edge.

Dirichlet-process regime clustering is explicitly rejected for production (label switching, versioning, MCMC cost, poor PROVEN audit) in favor of fixed sport|market groups + EB tau; the canonical data protocol is settled-only (never bootstrap, never seed), time-ordered train/holdout, scoring holdout Brier, ECE, Murphy REL/RES/UNC, log loss; never train ECE as publish proof.

Clean-room scoreboard-OCR spec: crop scoreboard-bug ROI (default top-left 320x90 + edge-density search) -> grayscale -> adaptive threshold -> 2x upscale -> OCR -> strict regexes /(\d)(?:ST|ND|RD|TH)\s*&\s*(\d+)/ for down & distance, /(\d):(\d\d)/ for clock, /(\d+)\s*-\s*(\d+)/ for score -> cross-check OCR LOS vs homography LOS (mismatch > 2 yards -> LOW confidence, not failure); parses '3RD & 7', 'Q2', '08:41', '17 - 14' into {down:3, distance:7, quarter:2, clockSec:521, scoreHome:17, scoreAway:14} at confidence >= 0.9; a garbage crop returns all-null, confidence 0, never throws.

Source fragility — sweeps run on read-only browser tasks with no API; @FTNData is protected, two timelines never render; X scraping at intake cadence is ToS-risky and CAPTCHA/rate-limit exposed. Two-stage architecture exists as described.
Stage 1 uses empirical target-ID via inverse-distance weighting on four distance measures.

The four distance measures are d^(1) point-to-ball-trajectory line distance, d^(2) standardized frame-difference, d^(3) frame-to-frame player-ball distance change, d^(4) Euclidean player-ball distance.
The weights are blended with adaptive weights W^(1..4) and a logistic frame-weight W^(2,3)_t = 1/(1+e^((13.34183−t)/2.57)).
The logistic frame-weight has an inflection at mean 13.34 frames, scale 2.57 via grid search.
Stage 2 uses conditional completion P(C|T=i) via random forest.
Marginal P(C) = Σ_i P(C|T=i)·P(T=i).

Baselines for target-ID accuracy: equal-weight 82.67%, W^(2) 86.68%, W^(3) 85.23%.

Week-to-week coefficient of variation of TopShare: CV = sd(TopShare_w) / mean(TopShare_w) over a rolling 4-week window. Module: qb-trust-target time series (feeds the qb-behavior module; shadow-first per Garrett's wire-first sequencing: research → wire → weight → calibrate → test → polish).
Inputs: nflverse pbp (existing ingestion), per season 2021–present (matches the triple criterion's window).

Outputs (per QB × week × situation): {qb_id, qb_name, season, week, situation, targets, distinct_receivers, hhi, n_eff, top_share, top2_share, top_share_cv_4wk, boot_hhi_lo, boot_hhi_hi} where situation ∈ {all, rz, third_down, two_min, trailing, pressured_proxy, quick_throw_proxy} per §3 filters.
Computation: single pass over pbp targets; group-by (qb, week, situation); bootstrap 1,000 resamples of plays within grain for HHI CIs. No new license, no new API, no founder gate.

Validation gates (pre-registered before first run): 1. Reproduce a known number: the pipeline must reproduce the Dynatyze WR1-feed league median (21% median WR1 target share, W1–W3 2026) within ±2pp from raw pbp — grounds the target definition against a third-party chart. 2. Triple-criterion backtest: recompute legs 2–3 (air-yard share, TPRR needs routes — charting; so backtest legs 1-proxy + 2 on pbp) and test whether the historical 64%/84.2%/92% ordering holds on GSE-owned data, 2021–2025. Leg 1 (true first-read) stays charted-only until the FTN join is stood up. 3. Stability gate: report week-to-week autocorrelation of hhi and top_share — if concentration doesn't persist, it's a descriptive stat, not a predictive feature, and ships as context only. 4. Anti-leakage: per the KONTOGRAPH invariant (c02 finding #20), every grain must be point-in-time (week w features use plays < week w kickoff); perturb-the-future property test on the week boundary.

Explicitly out of scope for v1: true first-read % (needs charting join — queue behind the FTN/PFF decision), Dirichlet-multinomial smoothing (adopt only if the stability gate shows small-sample blowups — then HHI gets a Dirichlet prior, α from the league median share vector; this is the principled place for the share model, not v1), coverage-shell splits (needs NGS coverage classification wiring, founder-gated).

Estimated shape: one ingestion-time aggregation job + one table; ~1 engineer-day to first shadow numbers, gated by the three validation checks above. The 25-target minimum, the bootstrap CIs, and the charted/pbp_proxy naming discipline are non-negotiable parts of the spec.

avgCushion (receiving) measures defender alignment distance at snap. It is strictly NGS-only.
avgSeparation (receiving) measures receiver separation at the catch point. It is strictly NGS-only.
avgYac (receiving) measures actual yards after catch. It is computable from pbp (mean(yards_after_catch) per receiver-week).
avgExpectedYac (receiving) measures expected YAC (tracking model). It is strictly NGS-only.
avgYacAboveExpectation (receiving) measures actual − expected YAC residual. It is strictly NGS-only.
catchPct (receiving) measures conversion. It is computable from pbp (sum(reception)/sum(targets) per receiver-week).
pctShareIntendedAirYards (receiving) measures target share of air yards. It is computable from pbp (sum(air_yards on targets) / team sum(air_yards on targets) per week).
avgTimeToThrow (passing) measures snap → release, seconds. It is strictly NGS-only. The critical gap (see BUILDABLE SPEC).
avgIntendedAirYards (passing) measures depth. It is computable from pbp (mean(air_yards) over pass attempts per passer-week).
avgCompletedAirYards (passing) measures depth on completions. It is computable from pbp (mean(air_yards) where complete_pass==1).
avgAirYardsToSticks (passing) measures depth relative to sticks. It is computable from pbp (INFERENCE: mean(air_yards − ydstogo) over attempts; approximates the NGS definition).

cpoe (passing) measures completion % over expected. It is computable from pbp with a naming caveat (mean(cpoe) of the nflverse pbp cpoe column per passer-week). CAVEAT: this is nflverse's own expected-completion model, NOT the NGS tracking model. Per the governing rule, name it cpoe_nflverse_pbp_*, never cpoe.

expectedCompletionPct (passing) measures model-expected completion %. It is computable from pbp (INFERENCE: Via the algebraic identity CPOE = comp% − xComp%: xComp ≈ completionPct − mean(cpoe) at the passer-week aggregate. INFERENCE: assumes the pbp cpoe column is present and additive-consistent).
completionPct (passing) measures completions / attempts. It is computable from pbp (sum(complete_pass)/sum(pass_attempt)).
aggressiveness (passing) measures throws into tight windows (<1 yd separation). It is strictly NGS-only. Proxies only (see BUILDABLE SPEC); name aggressiveness_proxy_*, never aggressiveness.
avgTimeToLos (rushing) measures snap → line of scrimmage, seconds. It is strictly NGS-only.

pctAttemptsGte8Defenders (rushing) measures stacked-box exposure rate. It is not computable from pbp. NOTE: the rights verdict says personnel/box counts are clean CC-BY-SA via FTN charting (load_ftn_charting() 2022+) — a cleared non-NGS route exists for this one.
rushYardsOverExpected (rushing) measures tracking-expected rushing residual. It is strictly NGS-only.
rushYardsOverExpectedPerAtt (rushing) measures RYOE per attempt. It is strictly NGS-only.
expectedRushYards (rushing) measures tracking-model expectation. It is strictly NGS-only.

Estimand definition: τ̂ = the quantile τ ∈ [0,1] of the next-state value distribution that makes observed 4th-down decisions minimally suboptimal under the τ-quantile MDP.

Forward model: one-period MDP, actions {GO, FGA, PUNT}; future play after t+1 follows fixed league-average stationary policy π̄ (a Markov reward process).
Rewards (Eq. 3.3): r(TD)=6.95 (6 + league-average conversion value), r(FG)=3, r(SAF)=−2; negated for team B.
Next-state value (Eq. 4.3): V^π̄_t(σ,a) := r(S_{t+1}(σ,a)) + E_π̄[Σ_{n=t+2}^{T} r(S_n) | S_{t+1}(σ,a)]. Value function via the infinite-horizon approximation of Chan, Fernandes and Puterman 2021.

Candidate objective (Eq. 4.6): q^π̄_τ(σ,a) = Q_τ[V^π̄(σ,a)] = inf{x : τ ≤ F_{V^π̄}(x|σ,a)}. Using the next-state value instead of the full return deliberately avoids assuming coaches use the same quantile in all future situations.
Transitions: empirical proportions p̂(s′|σ,a), p̂(s′|s,π̄) (Eq. 5.1–5.2); quantiles from the empirical next-state value distribution (Eq. 5.4).

Regularization: bivariate monotonic smoothing (SCAM, Pya & Wood 2015 tensor-product penalized B-splines, k=4 knots, monotonic-decreasing in yardline and yards-to-go); GO-transition augmentation with 3rd-down plays à la Romer 2006 to counter Daly-Grafstein 2023 selection bias.

Inverse problem: min_{τ∈[0,1]} (1/N)Σ_j 1(a_j ≠ a*_j(σ_j, q^π̄_τ)) — average Hamming loss between observed decisions and τ-optimal decisions (Eq. 4.11). Two-region version (Eq. 4.12); joint estimation of (τ_1, τ_2) (Eq. 5.5). L ≥ 3 partitions are underidentified given |A|=3 — hard ceiling at two regions.

Composition: for each 4th-down state, the engine computes (a) WP-optimal action, (b) τ̂-predicted action, (c) the WP-points gap between them.

The document specifies the exact systems the qb-behavior/ module implements, each traceable to verified claims.
A system is 'buildable' when its inputs exist, its formula is specified, and its validation gate is stated.

The proposal's Index 1 (sensitivity on a charted clean/pressured split) is unbuildable from nflverse because the nflverse FTN release has no per-play pressure field, pbp has only qb_hit, and pbp_participation.was_pressure is post-season-only.
The engine serves a floor construction, honestly named, and keeps the spec's charted Index 1 as NULL pending charting.
The phase-1 qb_hit-over-dropbacks team-week construction is NOT this system (wrong label, wrong grain).
The dropback grain is defined as qb_dropback == 1, REG only, exclude qb_kneel/qb_spike.
The pressured_floor is defined as qb_hit == 1 OR sack == 1, which is a floor construction because hurries are absent everywhere.
The clean condition is defined as NOT pressured_floor, which is contaminated because it contains unflagged hurries.
The formula for sensitivity_epa_floor is sensitivity_epa_floor(qb, grain) = mean(epa | clean) − mean(epa | pressured_floor).
equation: sensitivity_epa_floor(qb, grain) = mean(epa | clean) − mean(epa | pressured_floor)

claim: sensitivity_epa_floor is reported ALWAYS alongside mean(epa | clean) — the clean baseline, never the raw gap alone, because raw cross-QB ranking confounds fragility with QB quality.
int_rate_clean and int_rate_pressure_floor are EB-shrunk INT rates per the System 2 ladder, split on pressured_floor.
A minimum of 100 pressured dropbacks is required for the pressure-split engine, with small-sample refusal per a02 (never clamp).
The 100-guard overselects QBs in bad situations, so leaderboard views carry the caveat.
The clean cell contains unflagged hurries, so the clean−pressured contrast is biased TOWARD ZERO, meaning every served contrast is conservative (understated), never overstated.
The _floor suffix is mandatory for sensitivity_epa_floor, int_rate_pressure_floor, and clean_epa_baseline. Never bare 'pressure.' Never 'fragile' — neutral 'degradation'.
System 1 evaluates QBs under pressure. It NEVER projects sack totals (R² < 0.005). No predicted_sacks column exists in any output.
Report sensitivity_epa_floor, clean_epa_baseline, and protection_stress always — the QB's response, his baseline, and his protection context are a triple, never a lone number.
Validation: league-marginal pressure-floor rate reproduces across seasons within tolerance.
Validation: sensitivity is negative for ≥90% of QBs with n≥100 (pressure hurts — a sign check, not a value pin).
Validation: no FTN-derived column in engine outputs (rights acceptance, a06).
System 2 implements a03 INT recipe (display lane) + a06 buildable spec (engine lane); c02-r36 denoised-rate auditor method; occurrence-not-recovery rule.
The modeled quantity for System 2 is interception (actual occurrence — never margin, never worthy rate).
The cells for System 2 are pressure_floor × qtr × score_bucket × field_zone × down_distance.
The score_bucket dimension is {trail_8+, trail_1_7, tied, lead_1_7, lead_8+}.
The field_zone dimension is {own_1_25, mid, opp_25_21, redzone (yardline_100<=20)}.
The down_distance dimension is {early (1-2), late (3-4)} × {short ≤3, mid 4-7, long 8+}.
The estimation formula is cell = (w + M·p̂_parent)/(n + M), M=25, ladder league → team → QB, global→downward.
Floors: no leaf served at n<30 (auto back-off); no QB pressure split below 100 pressured dropbacks.
Pooling is 3 seasons, with regime-change reset on team/coach change (roster-break detection per projection_methods.md).
Output is E[INT_rate] per QB×cell + Poisson band; top contributing cells; NULLs where floors unmet.

The display lane danger-volume formula is expected_dropbacks × worthy_rate × 0.523 with stated bands; blitz splits via n_blitzers join (95% coverage guard); explicit 'single-game INTs are noise' labeling. Never enters training exports.
Regress realized INT counts toward the 46.3% league recovery mean before comparing danger vs results; model occurrence only.
Validation: league-marginal INT rate reproduces the nflverse marginal on a holdout season.
Validation: backed-off rates monotone-sensible where priors exist (trailing > leading).
Validation: resolveFeatureRights-style pin: no FTN-derived column in any training export.
System 3 implements a05 buildable spec; PRFFBall triple (re-implementation); FTN read_thrown validation lane.
The universe for System 3 is pass_attempt==1 AND receiver non-missing; exclude spikes; throwaways via FTN is_throw_away where joined (else kept, documented).
The trust-target system uses targets T, distinct receivers N, and shares s_i.
The formulas are hhi = Σ s_i², n_eff = 1/hhi, top_share = max s_i, top2_share = sum of top 2.
equation: hhi = Σ s_i² ; n_eff = 1/hhi ; top_share = max s_i ; top2_share = sum of top 2

claim: The trust stability metric is top_share_cv_4wk = sd/mean of top_share over rolling 4 weeks.
equation: top_share_cv_4wk = sd/mean of top_share over rolling 4 weeks

claim: Bootstrap HHI CI uses 1,000 resamples of plays within grain.
The minimum denominator is T ≥ 25 per grain (else NULL).

Backtest the historical ordering on 2021–2025 with pre-registered conditioning.

Validation gate: triple backtest ordering holds.

System 1b implements proposal Index 2. It is the buildable half of the pressure proposal — full PFR pressure taxonomy (hurries INCLUDED), team grain, no charting needed.
Inputs for System 1b are nflverse pfr_advstats, stat_type='pass', summary_level='week', 2018+): per team-week (REG only), QB rows summed: times_pressured, times_blitzed, dropback denominator.
Verify PFR's pressure dedup rule (pressured ≈ hurried+hit+sacked — confirm), PFR's blitz definition, the denominator of times_pressured_pct.
The formula for pressure_rate_allowed is pressure_rate_allowed = pressured_tw / dropbacks_tw.
The formula for blitz_rate_faced is blitz_rate_faced = blitzed_tw / dropbacks_tw.
The league fit is refit weekly, season-to-date: OLS pressure_rate_allowed ~ α + β·blitz_rate_faced.
The formula for protection_stress is protection_stress = pressure_rate_allowed − (α̂ + β̂·blitz_rate_faced), where + = losing 1v1s.

Guards for System 1b: < 3 team games → NULL; fit pool < 32 team-weeks → NULL for all teams (early-season null). Unweighted OLS is the literal read of 'linear'; intercept included; document both choices. Consider a fit-quality gate (|t(β)|>2) — owner call, not in spec.

Caveats for System 1b: blitz rate is endogenous (defenses choose it); QB-fault sacks inflate the line's number; quick-game scheme suppresses both rates. Display-only v1 per the proposal — 'No pick-engine input in v1.'

[c08 Deep Research — Buildable Systems | SYS-1. Correlated-thesis machinery (the funnel killer)] **Contract:** `correlatedTheses(legs, trace) → ThesisBundle[]`; `overconfidence(bundle) → {OR, n_eff}`. **Math:** `V_naive = Σσ²_i`; `V_true = w'Σw = Σσ²_i + 2Σ_{i<j}ρ_ij σ_i σ_j` (Bates–Granger MSFE form, 1675); `OR = V_true/V_naive`; `n_eff = n/(1+(n−1)ρ̄)`. **Detection:** Channel A — chain overlap on the trace (shared named link + overlapping falsifiers = same link). Channel B — PCA-strip common forecast errors → GL on idiosyncratic precision (τ>0 mandatory) → off-diagonal gives R (1675 recipe). Channel C — group-SCAD leg pruning before combining (1482). **Fusion choice:** CI (unknown correlation) / ICI (identifiable common structure — the funnel's canonical case) / CU (CONFLICT tracks) / never PW on shared-information sources. **Exposure:** bundle staked as ONE position — fused (ICI/CI) probability, Kelly on bundle edge under the 0822 30% drawdown governor; UI renders one thesis with combined exposure and n_eff; the four-receipts presentation is a contract violation. **Kill test:** the TNF funnel (4 legs, `pit_pressure_lands`) → one bundle, n_eff ≈ 1.1–1.5, verdict KILL. **Corpus:** 0790 (PW 0.11 vs ICI 0.48), 1675, 1482, spec §8 T1/T4.

[c08 Deep Research — Buildable Systems | SYS-2. Per-market abstention gate (1776 × 1151)] **Contract:** `perMarketAbstentionGate(p, q, market) → {FIRE | LEAN | ABSTAIN, reason_code, tiebreak_draw, per_class_errors}`. **Inputs:** calibrated p, market-implied q, market ∈ {spread,total,moneyline}, per-market caps from bankroll tolerance (re-fit quarterly), nonconformity s=1−max(p,1−p), market-conditional thresholds (α_m,β_m) grid-searched on chronological validation. **Invariants:** additive ambiguity ONLY (product banned — Phoneme R0=0.0551 precedent); randomized tie-breaking with logged seed; deterministic strict feasibility must never yield all-abstain; no class exceeds its cap in >1 of 4 walk-forward seasons (hard fail). **Kill test:** ≥15% lower abstention than the single global gate, all classes under cap, walk-forward; else REJECT. **v2:** re-derive the ambiguity objective in expected-unit terms (count-loss is v1 with the discrepancy logged). **Corpus:** 1776, 1151, 0211-gate discipline.

[c08 Deep Research — Buildable Systems | SYS-3. Deferral messaging + override contract] **Rule:** abstained matchups render "ENGINE ABSTAINS — low confidence" with NO lean, NO probability, NO interval. Analyst re-handicaps blind. **Override:** written justification ≥140 chars, reviewer-stamped, stored with the pick record. **Activation gate:** internal replication first — 40 abstained matchups, DO vs BM-style, per-analyst; pass = DO-style ≥ BM-style. Until then the rule is a hypothesis with a protocol. **Kill test:** replication fails to replicate direction → rule stays hypothesis, lean stays visible. **Corpus:** 1492 (direction survives, magnitudes don't).

[c08 Lane B — Adversarial Verification: Selective Prediction, Abstention, Distrust | CHALLENGES] **Challenge A — Per-class gates on correlated classes.** 1776 assumes classes with separately meaningful error constraints. In sports, spread and moneyline errors are correlated (same underlying game outcome; line moves together). Per-class caps on correlated classes can be *simultaneously* violated by the same bad week — the feasibility proof assumes the constraint structure, not the correlation structure. The build must measure inter-class error correlation before trusting per-class feasibility; if ρ(error_spread, error_ml) is high, the "separate caps" are one cap wearing a disguise, and the additive-ambiguity minimization is optimizing against a constraint set that binds jointly. Randomized tie-breaking at the boundary then becomes *coin-flip behavior on real-money decisions* — every draw must be logged with its seed, and the weekly share of draw-influenced decisions must be reported (BUILDABLE-6).

[c08 Lane B — Adversarial Verification: Selective Prediction, Abstention, Distrust | CHALLENGES] **Challenge B — The DO-messaging rule may reverse under experts.** 1492's subjects were lay image-labelers. An expert NFL analyst may *benefit* from seeing the engine lean (as a second opinion) more than they suffer from anchoring — expertise could flip the sign of the effect. The file anticipates this (`:52`: three-arm replication adding a confidence-armed arm). The adversary's stronger version: even the direction could differ by *reviewer*, making a standing policy wrong for some analysts. The internal replication must be run per-analyst, not pooled, or the policy is imposed on evidence about other people.

[c08 Lane B — Adversarial Verification: Selective Prediction, Abstention, Distrust | CHALLENGES] **Challenge C — LOPO's unit of generalization is unstable in sports.** 0211's pitchers are stable individuals; NFL "players" are not — they change teams, schemes, roles, and injury states across the 2023–2024 window the file proposes (`:54`). A LOPO test that holds out a player who changed teams mid-window confounds player-generalization with regime-generalization. The adversary demands the LOPO protocol stratify by regime-stability: report LOPO-within-stable-regime and LOPO-across-regime separately. A pooled-vs-LOPO gap driven by team changes is not evidence of player-memorization; it is evidence the features aren't regime-robust, which is a different defect with a different repair.

[c08 Lane B — Adversarial Verification: Selective Prediction, Abstention, Distrust | CHALLENGES] **Challenge E — Count-loss abstention misprices the actual decision.** 1776 minimizes abstention *count* subject to error-rate caps. In sports, a wrong posted pick costs units and a missed opportunity costs expected units — the decision is in *unit loss*, not counts. [Challenges — c10 HALF A (r01–r30) | A. Inflated or misleading numbers (the honest delta is smaller) | 1. r26/1516 — SEL features: 60.11% → 81.32% accuracy is a leakage signature, not a breakthrough] Claim: Random Forest accuracy jumps 21.2pp (60.11% → 81.32%, Brier 0.4837 → 0.3145) from two "strength of early lineup" features. Why challenged: the source file itself flags it (INFERENCE by the deep-read author): the paper does not state strengths were re-estimated strictly as-of each match date (expanding window). A 21-point jump from two features on a 250-game test set is the classic leakage shape. Also: single small test window (250 games, one sport/gender, three months), no opponent adjustment in strength estimation (unbalanced schedules), no CIs. Status: ADAPT with the numbers treated as **upper bounds achievable only with future information**. Rehabilitate: re-run expanding-window with as-of-date strength estimates; report the with/without-SEL delta on that run. The SEL *pattern* (early-lineup strength) is portable; the *numbers* are not. Source: `arxiv-program/research/2026-09-21/arxiv-deep/1516-prediction-of-handball-matches-with-statistically.md`

[Challenges — c10 HALF A (r01–r30) | A. Inflated or misleading numbers (the honest delta is smaller) | 2. r04/0178 — serve prediction 83.18% vs betting odds 69.04%: probable target leakage] Claim: RF 83.18% accuracy beats betting odds' 69.04%. Why challenged: the decisive serve features (FirstWonFirstIn, SecondWonSecondIn) have no stated pre-match aggregation window and appear sourced from per-match charting — i.e., the features likely contain the outcome being predicted. Odds still achieved the highest total confidence score (2059.66) despite lower accuracy, which is consistent with odds being calibrated and the RF being sharp-but-leaky. Status: **REJECT stays rejected.** Rehabilitate: pre-match-only feature windows, walk-forward evaluation, calibration comparison (not just accuracy).

The brief already makes this correction; the challenge is to anyone quoting the headline. Status: ADAPT, but the gate (≥0.01 AUC vs the **relativized twin**) exists precisely because of this. The three-layer staking stack] **Why this order:** Kelly sets the unconstrained growth rate; the governor enforces the drawdown constraint pathwise; CVaR penalizes both game variance (inner) and edge-estimation uncertainty (outer) — the latter is genuinely new capability: GSE has no edge-uncertainty penalty today. Dominant Asset screening (1213, other half) runs before Kelly: only play assets whose growth rate is robust to the edge-estimation noise CVaR-δ penalizes.

[Reasoning Depth Spec — NFL Intelligence Engine] **Created:** 2026-10-01/02, after Steelers @ Browns TNF (Browns 24, Steelers 16) **For:** Coding agent — post-audit build. Pairs with `tnf-intelligence-program-2026-10-01.md` (Tracks 1–3: QB profiles, coaching tendencies, trust-signal intake). **Status:** Spec. No code. Implementation-ready: data structures, API shape, test assertions.
[Reasoning Depth Spec — NFL Intelligence Engine | 1. Why this exists] Tonight's card went 4-4, and the four losses shared one failure mode: **the analysis was stat-deep but reasoning-shallow.**

[Reasoning Depth Spec — NFL Intelligence Engine | 1. Why this exists] The pressure-funnel stack (Watson under 187.5, game under 38.5, Watt over 0.5 sacks, both-teams-2+ FGs) was built on a true fact — Pittsburgh's pass rush vs Cleveland's injured interior OL — treated as physics. At halftime Watson was 14/17 for 181 yards, zero sacks, ~130 rating, Browns up 21-10. Final: Watson 223 yards (blew past the under), 24-16 Browns.
[Reasoning Depth Spec — NFL Intelligence Engine | 1. Why this exists] The counter-evidence **existed before kickoff** and was even quantified in tonight's own research track:
[Reasoning Depth Spec — NFL Intelligence Engine | 1. Why this exists] Todd Monken's 2026 quick-game proxy: **0.639** vs league average **0.508**
[Reasoning Depth Spec — NFL Intelligence Engine | 1. Why this exists] Average air yards: **8.33 → 6.12**; deep rate **0.120 → 0.060**
[Reasoning Depth Spec — NFL Intelligence Engine | 1. Why this exists] Early-down pass rate across the team switch: **0.424 → 0.562**

[Reasoning Depth Spec — NFL Intelligence Engine | 1. Why this exists] No reasoning layer connected "Monken throws it short and fast" to "the pass rush can't get home" to "the under thesis is dead." The data was in the building. Nothing walked it down the hall.

[Reasoning Depth Spec — NFL Intelligence Engine | 1. Why this exists] Garrett's directive: the engine needs **reasoning levels, depth of intelligence, and complex reasoning comparable to Grok 4.x** — applied over the full NFL intelligence corpus (inside the game, outside the game, around the game). This spec defines what that means, mechanically.

[Reasoning Depth Spec — NFL Intelligence Engine | 2. What "Grok 4.x-class reasoning" means — grounded mechanisms] Every mechanism below is a documented property of the Grok 4 model family. Each is mapped to its NFL-intelligence equivalent. Sources are listed in §9; claims without a cited source are marked SPEC (our design choice, not xAI's).

[Reasoning Depth Spec — NFL Intelligence Engine | 2. What "Grok 4.x-class reasoning" means — grounded mechanisms | 2.1 Thinking depth as a runtime dial (Grok 4.1 / 4.7)] **What xAI built:** Grok 4.1 ships two modes — a fast low-latency mode and a multi-step "Thinking" mode that spends extra reasoning tokens on hard problems (theaitrack.com; codecademy.com). Grok 4.5+ exposes `reasoning_effort` (`low` / `medium` / `high`, plus `xhigh` on 4.6/4.7) as an API-level depth lever; reasoning is built-in and cannot be disabled (prompt-atlas; anyaa-labs). Grok 4.7's training specifically targeted multi-step, multi-hour agentic flows and self-verification to cut hallucinations on extended knowledge work (i10x.ai).

[Reasoning Depth Spec — NFL Intelligence Engine | 2. What "Grok 4.x-class reasoning" means — grounded mechanisms | 2.1 Thinking depth as a runtime dial (Grok 4.1 / 4.7)] **NFL equivalent:** Reasoning depth is not a vibe — it is a **budgeted, selectable parameter** on every engine analysis. A Tuesday-morning futures scan can run shallow; a Sunday card with real exposure runs at maximum depth. The engine must support at least four depth tiers and must route automatically (see §4).

[Reasoning Depth Spec — NFL Intelligence Engine | 2. What "Grok 4.x-class reasoning" means — grounded mechanisms | 2.2 Multi-agent parallel reasoning with debate (Grok 4 Heavy / 4.20)] **What xAI built:** Grok 4 Heavy spawns multiple specialized agents per query — e.g., one for research, one for code, one for data analysis — coordinated by a higher-level controller that synthesizes (macaron.im; medium.com). Grok 4.20 runs four named specialized agents that think in parallel and **debate each other in real time** before a captain agent aggregates the strongest elements and resolves conflicts; contradictions are caught before output, which xAI credits for the hallucination reduction (nextbigfuture.com).

[Reasoning Depth Spec — NFL Intelligence Engine | 2. What "Grok 4.x-class reasoning" means — grounded mechanisms | 2.2 Multi-agent parallel reasoning with debate (Grok 4 Heavy / 4.20)] **NFL equivalent:** No single reasoning pass produces a pick. For any bet recommendation at depth ≥ L3, the engine runs **parallel specialist tracks** — at minimum:

[Reasoning Depth Spec — NFL Intelligence Engine | 2. What "Grok 4.x-class reasoning" means — grounded mechanisms | 2.2 Multi-agent parallel reasoning with debate (Grok 4 Heavy / 4.20)] `stat-agent` [Numbers: lines, splits, rates PIT pressure rate, CLE OL injuries]

[Reasoning Depth Spec — NFL Intelligence Engine | 2. What "Grok 4.x-class reasoning" means — grounded mechanisms | 2.2 Multi-agent parallel reasoning with debate (Grok 4 Heavy / 4.20)] `scheme-agent` [Coaching/scheme layer Monken quick-game 0.639, air yards 6.12]

[Reasoning Depth Spec — NFL Intelligence Engine | 2. What "Grok 4.x-class reasoning" means — grounded mechanisms | 2.2 Multi-agent parallel reasoning with debate (Grok 4 Heavy / 4.20)] `behavior-agent` [QB behavioral profile Watson INT-under-pressure splits; Rodgers trust-target HHI]

[Reasoning Depth Spec — NFL Intelligence Engine | 2. What "Grok 4.x-class reasoning" means — grounded mechanisms | 2.2 Multi-agent parallel reasoning with debate (Grok 4 Heavy / 4.20)] `signal-agent` [Trust signals / news Rodgers–Metcalf video; injury reports]

[Reasoning Depth Spec — NFL Intelligence Engine | 2. What "Grok 4.x-class reasoning" means — grounded mechanisms | 2.2 Multi-agent parallel reasoning with debate (Grok 4 Heavy / 4.20)] `adversary-agent` [Kill the thesis "What breaks the pressure funnel?" (see §4, L4)]

[Reasoning Depth Spec — NFL Intelligence Engine | 2. What "Grok 4.x-class reasoning" means — grounded mechanisms | 2.2 Multi-agent parallel reasoning with debate (Grok 4 Heavy / 4.20)] A **synthesizer** resolves conflicts with explicit precedence rules (§5). The adversary-agent is mandatory, not optional — it is the structural fix for tonight.

[Reasoning Depth Spec — NFL Intelligence Engine | 2. What "Grok 4.x-class reasoning" means — grounded mechanisms | 2.3 Self-verification loops (Grok 4.7)] **What xAI built:** Grok 4.7's training emphasized self-verification on long agentic flows; parallel tool use lets the model cross-check as it works (i10x.ai; venturebeat.com). In the 4.20 council, one agent's role is active verification of the others' claims before synthesis (nextbigfuture.com).

[Reasoning Depth Spec — NFL Intelligence Engine | 2. What "Grok 4.x-class reasoning" means — grounded mechanisms | 2.3 Self-verification loops (Grok 4.7)] **NFL equivalent:** Every factual claim in a reasoning trace carries a **verification status**: `CORPUS` (sourced from ingested data), `COMPUTED` (derived by engine code, reproducible), `SINGLE_SOURCE` (one outlet, uncorroborated), `INFERENCE` (model judgment, flagged). [Reasoning Depth Spec — NFL Intelligence Engine | 4. Reasoning levels L1–L5 | L1 — Direct lookup] **What:** Answer from a single profile, table, or line. No cross-referencing.

[Reasoning Depth Spec — NFL Intelligence Engine | 4. Reasoning levels L1–L5 | L1 — Direct lookup] **Auto-escalates to L2 when:** the question involves a matchup (two entities), a line vs a number, or any injury/lineup flag is present.
[Reasoning Depth Spec — NFL Intelligence Engine | 4. Reasoning levels L1–L5 | L2 — Cross-stat correlation] **What:** Two or more signals combined; correlations and splits surfaced.

[Reasoning Depth Spec — NFL Intelligence Engine | 4. Reasoning levels L1–L5 | L2 — Cross-stat correlation] **Example:** "Watson's INT rate under pressure vs clean, by quarter and score state" (Track 1 output). "Monken quick-game rate vs league average."

[Reasoning Depth Spec — NFL Intelligence Engine | 4. Reasoning levels L1–L5 | L2 — Cross-stat correlation] **Output:** correlated findings + the joint table + which correlations are computed vs asserted.

[Reasoning Depth Spec — NFL Intelligence Engine | 4. Reasoning levels L1–L5 | L2 — Cross-stat correlation] **Auto-escalates to L3 when:** a bet recommendation is requested; or the L2 output contains a **causal claim** ("pressure will overwhelm the OL"); or two L2 signals disagree (stat-agent vs scheme-agent conflict).

[Reasoning Depth Spec — NFL Intelligence Engine | 4. Reasoning levels L1–L5 | L3 — Causal chain] **What:** Explicit cause → mechanism → outcome chains, each link sourced. Scheme → adjustment → outcome.

[Reasoning Depth Spec — NFL Intelligence Engine | 4. Reasoning levels L1–L5 | L3 — Causal chain] **Example:** "CLE interior OL injuries → Monken shifts to quick game (0.639 rate, 6.12 air yards, Weeks 1–3) → PIT pressure rate projects below its season average → Watson dropback EPA holds → under 187.5 requires a deep-dropback game script that Monken hasn't run all season."

[Reasoning Depth Spec — NFL Intelligence Engine | 4. Reasoning levels L1–L5 | L3 — Causal chain] **Requirements:** every link carries verification status; any `INFERENCE` link is flagged; the chain lists its **breaking conditions** (the observable facts that would falsify each link).

[Reasoning Depth Spec — NFL Intelligence Engine | 4. Reasoning levels L1–L5 | L3 — Causal chain] **Auto-escalates to L4 when:** real exposure is attached (a published pick, a card, anything Garrett could bet); or the L3 chain's conclusion contradicts the market by more than a threshold (SPEC: |edge| > 5% implied); or any link is `INFERENCE`/`SINGLE_SOURCE`.
[Reasoning Depth Spec — NFL Intelligence Engine | 4. Reasoning levels L1–L5 | L4 — Adversarial] **What:** A dedicated adversary-agent attempts to kill the L3 thesis. Mandatory outputs:

[Reasoning Depth Spec — NFL Intelligence Engine | 4. Reasoning levels L1–L5 | L4 — Adversarial] **The breaking-condition check:** are tonight's falsifiers already true? (Tonight: yes — TTT/quick-game thresholds met pre-kickoff.)

[Reasoning Depth Spec — NFL Intelligence Engine | 4. Reasoning levels L1–L5 | L4 — Adversarial] **Correlated-thesis detection:** do multiple recommended legs share one causal link? If yes, they are bundled as ONE thesis with combined exposure, never presented as independent edges.
[Reasoning Depth Spec — NFL Intelligence Engine | 4. Reasoning levels L1–L5 | L4 — Adversarial] **The strongest counter-argument,** steelmanned with numbers, not dismissed.
[Reasoning Depth Spec — NFL Intelligence Engine | 4. Reasoning levels L1–L5 | L4 — Adversarial] **Pre-mortem:** "It is Monday and this card went 0-4. What happened?" — written before the games.

[Reasoning Depth Spec — NFL Intelligence Engine | 4. Reasoning levels L1–L5 | L4 — Adversarial] **Auto-escalates to L5 when:** the adversary cannot kill the thesis (it survives → needs full synthesis); or the card contains 3+ legs; or Garrett requests "the full picture."

The GSE prop-projection INT recipe decomposes a QB's interception expectation as expected dropbacks times his FTN interception-worthy throw rate times the league worthy-to-INT conversion of 52.3%: Allen projected 27.0 expected dropbacks x 3.66% worthy rate (17 worthy in 464 dropbacks, 2025) x 0.523 = 0.5 INTs with a 0-2 band, Goff 34.2 x 1.44% (8 in 554) x 0.523 = 0.3 with a 0-1 band; the doctrine treats the QB's worthy rate (danger volume) as the persistent signal and the actual INT count as noisy realization (Allen 17 worthy vs 10 actual).
equation: E[INT_game] = expected_dropbacks x (interception-worthy throws / dropbacks) x 0.523

claim: Pressure generation is sticky but pressure-to-sack conversion is luck (R^2 < 0.005), so the props methodology deliberately ships NO single-game sack projection for any player (deliberate NULL); pressure stats (QB hits) may be shown as sticky pressure but the sack column stays empty.

Garbage-time correction: every volume projection is multiplied by the measured unfiltered/filtered per-game ratio for that exact stat, ranging 1.025-1.195 across stats (Allen attempts 1.025 moving 195 to 201, LaPorta targets 1.195 moving St. Brown receptions 6.5 to 8.0); the filter excludes about 11% of plays (garbage = qtr==4 AND (wp>0.95 OR wp<0.05), OT kept).

Measured 2025 dropback rates by possession-WP bucket: BUF leading (wp>0.65) 50.0% (n=328), neutral 57.2%, trailing (wp<0.35) 61.8%, season 56.3%; DET leading 54.2% (n=284), neutral 57.1%, trailing 68.2%, season 59.5%; matchup script assumed BUF 53% and DET 63%, moving Allen -14 and Goff +13 pass yards vs flat averages.

The 52.3% worthy-to-INT conversion is stated exactly once in the source as a single league-wide constant with no denominator, no sample size, and no situational split, making it unverifiable and unreconditionable from the document as given.

The props methodology's standing rate rule: efficiency levels are never blended (100% prior season / 0% current week for rates); the current week is a role-continuity check and structural-break flag only.
The Sion Vaki rule: no projections on players with no prior-season filtered sample - nominal RB2 by Week 1 usage but zero 2025 filtered touches gets NULL, no projectable role.

Allen scramble composition measured descriptively: 45 of his 89 rushes were scrambles, producing 387 of 543 rush yards (71%); his rushing projection is a pressure-plus-script derivative, not a designed-run projection.

The source doc's own stated limit: single-game INTs are Poisson noise, so any situational INT model must output wide bands and be scored over large samples; game-count point estimates without bands are theater.

nflverse qb_hit and sack_rate are explicitly lower-bound pressure proxies because hurries are invisible in the data; qb_hit undercounts true pressure and any pressure-conditioned model on nflverse alone inherits this blind spot.

No INT-by-situation splits exist in the verified props source: zero measured INT rates by pressure, quarter, score, field position, or down/distance (verified by full-file grep); the recipe produces a baseline-only scalar rate.

The pressure-sensitivity veto is narrow: it kills sack-count prediction, not pressure as an evaluative feature; the doc treats pressure as real and sticky (Goff's 18.9% hit rate, 2nd-highest allowed, used as stated downside risk on his efficiency) - pressure predicts pressure and QB response to it, not whether a hit becomes a sack.
